messages.content:
An adult education centre is running two craft workshops on Saturday. The morning class has 18 participants, and the afternoon class has 22. Each participant needs one complete kit containing a brush, a cloth, and two blank tiles. Brushes and cloths can be reused between classes only after cleaning. Tiles are consumable and cannot be reused. Cleaning one batch takes 40 minutes, regardless of how many brushes and cloths it contains, and the cleaning station can hold at most 15 brushes and 15 cloths per batch.

The morning class ends at 12:10. The afternoon class starts at 13:30. There are 24 brushes, 26 cloths, and 84 blank tiles in storage. Four brushes have damaged handles and cannot be used. Three cloths are reserved for cleaning the room and should not be allocated to participants. Two tiles are chipped and unusable. The available counts must exclude those items. Cleaned brushes and cloths become available only when a whole batch finishes. The cleaning station can process only one batch at a time.

The organiser proposes using 18 brushes and 18 cloths in the morning, leaving the rest clean for the afternoon. At 12:10, volunteers can immediately start cleaning the used items. They do not need time to transport them to the station, and loading and unloading are already included in the 40-minute batch duration. The afternoon class needs all kits ready by 13:25 so volunteers can place them on tables. This is a readiness deadline five minutes before the class starts. No participant can share a brush or a cloth during a class.

The centre can borrow up to four clean brushes and four clean cloths from a neighbouring studio. These borrowed items arrive at 13:00. The studio asks that any unused items be returned clean, while used items can be returned on Monday. Borrowing does not change the number of blank tiles. The organiser wants to borrow as few items as possible. There is no restriction that the number of borrowed brushes and cloths must be equal, but every kit still needs one of each.

A colleague claims there is enough time for two cleaning batches because there are 80 minutes between 12:10 and 13:30. Another says the five-minute setup margin changes the answer. A third thinks the tile supply is short because 18 plus 22 participants need 80 tiles and two are damaged. Check these statements using the available stock of 84 tiles, rather than treating 84 as the usable total. The centre cannot speed up the cleaning station, start cleaning before the morning class ends, or delay the afternoon setup.

Determine whether the workshops can run with the original stock and schedule. If borrowing is needed, calculate the smallest number of brushes and cloths to borrow and describe a feasible cleaning plan. Give the tile calculation separately. State the key time boundary that prevents an incorrect solution.
